gold_note: Intended reading: the Capitol/Congress sat in Philadelphia, PA until 1800 (Capitol article: 'first session ... November 17, 1800'), so 1887 (first 'official' Groundhog Day) - 1800 = 87. But the Phil article says he has made prognostications 'since 1886', which gives 86. The riddle-like wording (the Capitol is in DC, not a state) makes it underspecified; all three systems failed.
judge_note: No system produced 86/87; judges correct relative to gold.
pipeshub_root_cause: The model took 'same state as the US capitol' literally as Washington DC and substituted a different groundhog (Potomac Phil, DC, 2012) to compute 2012-1886=126, which does not answer the question about Punxsutawney Phil. The Capitol article (which has the Philadelphia/1800 history) was never retrieved, and the model did not search for the Capitol's history before answering after one fetch. Oracle, holding the Capitol article, also failed, so the main blocker is the question's interpretation.
evidence_snippet: Phil article: 'this one groundhog has lived to make weather prognostications since 1886'; Capitol article: 'the Capitol held its first session of the U.S. Congress ... on November 17, 1800'
best_rag_note: Had both articles but declined ('Cannot be determined'); did not consider the pre-1800 Philadelphia seat of Congress.
oracle_note: Had full articles but answered 'not enough information'; the puzzle needs the historical-capital interpretation.
generic_fix: Prompt rule: do not satisfy a constraint by substituting a different, similarly named entity (Potomac Phil for Punxsutawney Phil); if a literal reading makes the question impossible, try the historically or temporally plausible reading and search for it before answering. Small expected gain, since the question itself is underspecified.

gold_note: Chelsea last won the UCL in 2021 (London club); the World Cup holder then was France (2018). 'As of August 1, 2024' only fixes which London win is 'last'.
judge_note: PipesHub answered Argentina (2024 holder); correctly marked wrong.
pipeshub_root_cause: The question was parsed wrongly: the model applied the 'as of Aug 1, 2024' date to the World Cup holder instead of to the time of Chelsea's 2021 win. Both facts it needed (Chelsea 2021, France winning 2018) were in its evidence; it searched for the 2024 holder and stopped after two searches. Missing London article was irrelevant.
evidence_snippet: evidence l.940: 'the 2006, 2010, 2014, and 2018 tournaments all won by UEFA teams (Italy, Spain, Germany, and France, respectively)'
best_rag_note: Same mis-anchoring; said the sources do not give the holder at that time (NOT_ATTEMPTED), although the FIFA article was in its context.
oracle_note: Correct: linked Chelsea 2021 to France 2018.
generic_fix: Before the final answer, a planning/verification rule: for nested temporal questions ('the last time X happened, who was Y'), write down the reference date of each hop (Y is evaluated at the date of X, not at the question's as-of date) and check the answer against it.

gold_note: Gold 11,300,000 = 2011 built-up-area figures (Greater London BUA 9,787,426 + Liverpool 864,122 + Sheffield 685,368 = 11,336,916). City-proper figures give ~9.2M. The gold England article text in the corpus contains none of these city figures (only 9,787,426 for London's urban area), so the gold is not derivable from the gold articles alone.
judge_note: Judges correctly applied the gold; the gold's choice of urban-area vs city-proper is the ambiguity.
pipeshub_root_cause: Birthplaces were found correctly. Search returned the built-up-area figures that produce the gold (Northern_England blocks 49/51, London blocks 28/155), but the model chose city-proper figures 466,415 and 552,698 from its own memory. Those numbers appear nowhere in the evidence. It then ran about 10 searches using those remembered numbers as query terms ('Liverpool 2011 census 466,415') to try to confirm them, never found them, and answered with them anyway. The answer has no citation for any population figure.
evidence_snippet: Evidence has 'Rank: 3, Area: Liverpool, Population: 864,122' and 'Rank: 5, Area: Sheffield, Population: 685,368' (Northern_England) and London urban area '9,787,426 people in 2011'; '466,415' and '552,698' never appear.

oracle_note: Wrong (not attempted). The gold articles in this corpus lack the city 2011 figures, so it correctly said it could not compute.
generic_fix: Grounding rule enforced in the answer step: every number used in a calculation must come from a shown block and carry a citation. When the model's searches for a specific remembered value come back empty, it must use the closest figure the evidence does give (and name its definition, e.g. urban area) or say the value is missing. Add a post-answer check that flags uncited numerals that do not appear in the evidence.

gold_note: Zara Tindall, born 15 May 1981, was 41 on 8 Sep 2022, and 41-7=34. She is the eldest granddaughter; the granddaughters Beatrice (1988), Eugenie (1990) and Louise (2003) are younger.
judge_note: PipeShub said 'cannot calculate'; correctly marked wrong.
pipeshub_root_cause: The Elizabeth II 'Issue' table was flattened into row blocks where the 'Children'/'Grandchildren' columns mean the row person's (Anne's) children and grandchildren, i.e. the Queen's grandchildren and great-grandchildren. The block reads 'Name: Anne, Princess Royal ... Children: Peter Phillips, Grandchildren: * Savannah Phillips', and the model took Savannah as the Queen's eldest granddaughter. It then explicitly rejected Zara Tindall, whose 15 May 1981 birth date was in front of it, and spent 14 LLM calls and roughly 15 searches hunting Savannah's birth date, which is not in the corpus, before giving up. The table rows also lack the caption ('Issue of Elizabeth II'), and spanned cells are duplicated across rows 126 and 127.
evidence_snippet: Elizabeth_II (block 126): 'Name: Anne, Princess Royal ... Children: Peter Phillips, Grandchildren: * Savannah Phillips' ; Zara_Tindall: 'Zara Anne Elizabeth Tindall (née Phillips; born 15 May 1981)... She is a granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II'
best_rag_note: Got Zara's article and DOB in the context and computed 41-7=34 correctly.
oracle_note: Had all family articles; identified Zara (b. 1981) as the eldest granddaughter and gave 34.
generic_fix: Parser: give each table-row block the table caption and section heading (e.g. 'Issue of Elizabeth II > row: Anne'), so relative columns like Children/Grandchildren are anchored to the row subject. Prompt rule: when an explicit source statement ('She is a granddaughter of X') conflicts with an inference from a table, prefer the explicit statement or check the conflict before discarding a candidate.

gold_note: Finale 2013; the Best Director Oscar presented in 2013 (85th ceremony, Feb 2013) went to Ang Lee for Life of Pi. Slightly ambiguous because film-year 2013 gives Cuarón, but 'won ... the same year' most naturally means the award was won in 2013.
judge_note: Cuarón (86th, presented 2014) correctly marked wrong.
pipeshub_root_cause: PipesHub read the Best Director table row 'Year: 2013 (86th) Alfonso Cuarón' and took the film-eligibility year as the year the award was won. The 86th ordinal showed it was the 2014 ceremony, but the model did not check, and the 2012 (85th) row with Ang Lee was never shown. The 85th Academy Awards record was never retrieved.
evidence_snippet: evidence l.420-422: 'Academy_Award_for_Best_Director (block 450) Year: 2013 (86th), Director(s): **Alfonso Cuarón**' ; article: '2012 (85th) | Ang Lee | Life of Pi'

oracle_note: Had the 85th Academy Awards article (ceremony in 2013), so it answered Ang Lee.
generic_fix: Add a prompt rule: when the year in a table could mean either the period covered or the date the event happened (award or fiscal tables, for example), work out which one the column means before matching it to an event date. Also, search for the event record itself (for example, the specific ceremony) rather than relying only on the summary table.

pipeshub_root_cause: All records were fetched, and Iván Rodríguez block 81 (one-day contract, retiring as a Ranger) was in the prefetch evidence. The model replaced the question's literal predicate 'retired from' with the proxy 'last MLB team' and said so up front. Only fall back to a proxy when no literal match exists, and flag the fallback.
